neighborhood_overview:
This street is a beautifully tree lined street which runs right up the the entrance of the Phoenix Park.
This park is the largest urban park in Europe and houses Dublin Zoo and the presidential home and offices as well as a children's playground. It is a wonderful park to visit and spans over 1750 acres.
The street also has beautiful Victorian red bricked houses all along it which date back to the 18th century so it really is a taste of old Dublin.
There is a major supermarket just 3 minutes walk as well as a pharmacy, bakery, coffee shops, bars, restuarants and many other amenities all within easy walking distance.

I have been in the buidling trade for the last 20 years so I thought I would combine the two and refurbish the house and provide rental accommodation in an extremely convenient locations to tourists.

name: Best location in Dublin City Centre
description:
This listing is suitable for the young or young at heart! Two indoor cats live here. Small cosy double room with private terrace attached.

Bed is a 4’6/ 1.35m/ standard double. Original floorboards. Shower room is shared with us. The house is a redbrick artisan house, heart of the city centre, quiet street. Location location location. Cafes, pubs, restaurants nearby. 3 minute walk from Jury’s Inn Christchurch or Radisson Golden Lane hotels. Walk everywhere!
neighborhood_overview: I love this area.  Trinity College is a ten minute walk. as is Grafton Street and Camden St.  The location cannot be beaten.  I love my street as it is friendly and tree-lined.  The convenience cannot be overestimated.   The neighbourhood is a great  Love being able to walk everywhere, and feeling part of history in Dublin's most historic residential quarter.mix of traditional Dublin and hipster gentrification.
host_about:
Hello.  I am a professional living in Dublin city centre with my husband.   I have lived abroad and love to travel.  My interests include food, cinema, reading and spending time with friends.  We love having people over for dinner and meeting new people.    We also love eating out.

Of the places I have visited for pleasure, I especially loved India, Bali, Brazil, Bolivia, Laos and Japan.  I really enjoy meeting people when I travel she getting local recommendations.  I love all of the Mediterranean and Hong Kong.  I love reading anything set in India or anything by Douglas Kennedy, Anne Tyler.  My monthly book club is something I really look forward to.

We have really enjoyed meeting new people through Airbnb.  We are pretty passionate about Dublin, and like to share all the places that we think are special with visitors.   Edgar says that Dubliners can be the most friendly people in the world!

We now have 2 cats living with us.   The cats will be on holiday when you rent our home.

name: Very Special Oval Georgian Studio
description: Experience authentic Georgian elegance is this unique large OVAL studio apartment, overlooking park.  Accommodates two in cosy sleeping loft. Cook dinner in the designer kitchen, and then head out to enjoy the attractions of the city.
neighborhood_overview:
A beautiful, historic residential square, built in 1790's, within 5-10 minutes walk of down-town city centre. Elegance and convenience combined with a bit of inner city grittiness. I have loved it all, since 1978!

Mountjoy Square is situated just NE of the historic city centre, within walking distance of just about all the main city attractions. It is the most densely populated area in the entire city: 1500 people have front doors opening onto the Square.

The house fronts onto a 4acre/1.5ha park, across a fairly busy street. This apartment faces the side street, so it is quieter, but you will still hear traffic.....Please bear in mind that this is NOT LEAFY SUBURBIA, but a vibrant, living city community and it's definitely gritty in places... Having said that, I have lived here, uneventfully, for nearly 38 years, and consider the trade-offs well worth it, for the excitement and convenience of having the city on my doorstep..
host_about: Architectural enthusiast & committed urbanite, Alexander technique teacher, daily swimmer. I love to cook and to share meals with friends, and I aspire  to grow at least some of my own food. I love where I live, and enjoy all the amenities the city has to offer. I am Secretary of the Mountjoy Square Society, whose aim is to improve our area for all who live work and visit here. I am also a committee member of the Irish Georgian Society, and I regularly organize  day trips and walking tours for our members.

description:

8 minutes walk from Guinness, a 10 min bus ride will bring you into the heart of the city centre, or 25-30 min walk to the Trinity College entrance. Bus - 1 min, and tram - 8 mins walk from the house.

The area of Dublin 8 is a local neighbourhood, near the city Centre. It is a residential area with a lidl supermarket, cafe, launderette, hairdresser and a pharmacy close by.
A ten minute walk will get you to some good bars and cafes, and a street for antiques, and a 10 minute bus, or 25 minute walk will get you into the heart of the city centre , with bars, restaurants, music, etc. Trinity College is another 5 mins.
Dublin city centre is relatively small so everything is very close and walkable. The bus is a minute away and the Luas (tram) is 8 minutes away fron the house.

neighborhood_overview:
This street is a beautifully tree lined street which runs right up the the entrance of the Phoenix Park.
This park is the largest urban park in Europe and houses Dublin Zoo and the presidential home and offices as well as a children's playground. It is a wonderful park to visit and spans over 1750 acres.
The street also has beautiful Victorian red bricked houses all along it which date back to the 18th century so it really is a taste of old Dublin.
There is a major supermarket just 2 minutes walk as well as a pharmacy, bakery, coffee shops, bars, restuarants and many other amenities all within easy walking distance.

This is a very unique property on the beach front with direct access to the beach with stunning sea views. The apartment is in an idyllic location
with views of the sea. It is the perfect base for city & countryside touring. Location is suitable for relaxation & adventure. Imagine strolling along the beach with the moon shining on the sea or seeing the early morning sunrise coming up over the sea.
neighborhood_overview:
Rush was a small fishing village & is now a bustling seaside town. It has two beaches one of which the property is located on. This beach has lovely golden sand and is safe to swim in. At one end are cliffs with a Martello Tower & the other end is the harbour & local village. The village has much to offer in eating & drinking. There is also a local theatre, sailing & golf club

Dublin city centre with all its attractions is only a short train or car journey away (30 minutes)

We are also only 30 minutes to the famous Newgrange heritage site and the Hill of Tara

As we are on the east coast of Ireland the weather is mainly dry and mild.

Facilities in the local village include
Theatre
Sailing Club
Links Golf course
6 Restaurants
7 Pubs, some of which have live music and serve food
2 Supermarkets (Eurospar & Tesco) & many smaller retail business

Whelans, Dublin's most important music venue is around the corner on Wexford Street. Pub-of-the-year winners Devitt's is even closer and also has live music every night.

Other places of interest in the immediate vicinity include: St Patrick's Cathedral, Marsh's Library, the National Concert Hall, the Museum of Literature (MoLI), the Grand Canal, the Iveagh Gardens, St Stephen's Green … and many more.

Grafton Street, Trinity College, the Parliamentary buildings, the National History Museum and the National Gallery are within a radius of 10-15 mins walk. So too are Dublin Castle and the wonderful Chester Beattie Library.

The thriving nightlife of George's Street, South William Street and Dame Lane – and the more tourist-focused Temple Bar are within 15mins walk.

neighborhood_overview:
Our neighbourhood is in one of the best locations in Dublin. Site seeing tour bus stop located adjacent to house.
It takes 15 minutes to walk to Grafton Street and Trinity College or along the canal and visit the pubs favoured by many of our Irish poets and writers. Theatres, the Aviva Stadium and the docklands are just a stroll away.
Dublin bikes are available to hire at budget rates and well worth it. There are excellent pubs and restaurants to suit all tastes. Parks, museums and galleries all within a short stroll.
Herbert Park -
Next door Herbert Park is a green oasis spread over 32 acres of prime Ballsbridge land. It is named after Sidney Herbert, the father of the Earl of Pembroke who owned the land that Ballsbridge was built on. Some features of the park date back to the Dublin International Trades Exhibition, a kind of mini World Fair held in Dublin in 1907. name: Dublin-Killiney-Period Villa-Room 2of2 + Breakfast
description: Beautiful private bedroom(+shared Guest bathroom),in restored Georgian Villa in historic picturesque Killiney, South Dublin- with continental style breakfast. Located in a quiet neighbourhood at foot of Killiney Hill,near Killiney Bay/ beach. Easy access to  Dublin City, Dalkey and Dublin/Wicklow Mountains. Walking distance to DART (train-35/37mins to City Centre)+ bus services to Dun Laoghaire/Dublin City etc  and near to  LUAS(tram-Green Line) and  a Dublin Airport Aircoach  702 at Dalkey
neighborhood_overview:
Our period home is located in a quiet neighbourhood at the base of Killiney Hill. This is in the historic area of Killiney with it's many period houses. It is near to the splendid Killiney Bay with its European Blue Flag accredited beach that will suit hardy swimmers- there are bookable saunas on the beach that are ideal for pre or post swim use. For the less intrepid it is still a wonderful place to go for a stroll.
The historic Heritage Town of Dalkey is nearby. With it's numerous restaurants and bars and added to it's literary past it is a place well worth a visit-from our home it is just a short one stop hop away on the DART. For the more strenuous guests a lengthy walk to Dalkey could take in Killiney Hill and it's obelisk together with the spectacular 360deg panoramic views-these include views of: Killiney Bay from Dalkey to Bray Head( that has been rightly likened to Sorrento Bay in Italy), to the Sugarloaf Mountains in County Wicklow and to Dublin Bay and Dublin City.
host_about:

neighborhood_overview:
Rathmines (Irish: Ráth Maonais, meaning 'ringfort of Maonas') is an inner suburb on the Southside of Dublin in Ireland.
It lies three kilometres south of the city centre. It begins at the southern side of the Grand Canal and stretches along the Rathmines Road as far as Rathgar to the south, Ranelagh to the east, and Harold's Cross to the west.
It is situated in the city's D06 postal district.

Rathmines is served by the Luas light rail system: Ranelagh on the Green Line is the most convenient for access to the main street, while the Charlemont and Beechwood stops are also within walking distance of the area.

Dublin Bus routes 14, 15, 15A, 15B, 18, 65, 65B, 83, 140 and 142 serve Rathmines. The area is also served by the Dublin Bus Nitelink routes 15N and 49N on Friday and Saturday nights and on public holidays.

name: Period Home in Dublin 9
description:
Enjoy a stay in our charming 3-bedroom house in the heart of Dublin's Drumcondra!

Enjoy the convenience of local cafes, restaurants, supermarkets, shops and pubs on your doorstep. With well-connected public transport options to bring you to Dublin city centre (15 mins) or the airport (20 mins). Our spacious home features a living room, modern kitchen, and comfortable bedrooms. Perfect for both families and those who wish to experience Dublin and a local neighbourhood!
neighborhood_overview:
Drumcondra (Irish: Droim Conrach, meaning 'Conra's Ridge') is a residential area and inner suburb on the Northside of Dublin. It is a traditional leafy suburban village with a modern social scene shared between trendy bars, bistros and vintage pubs.

The area is friendly and tranquil, and with one of Dublin's universities nestled in multiple locations around the area, there is plenty of live and energy to the neighborhood. Just a 20-minute walk to O'Connell Street and a short drive to Dublin Airport.

Drumcondra is well serviced by public transport and it's very easy to hail a taxi. In more recent times, the area has become popular with younger professionals and students from the nearby DUBLIN UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY and The King's Inn Law School.

The area is generally safe and quiet. Weekends can be a little busier, but this is to be expected as people make their way home after socializing in the city centre.

description: Treat yourself & stay at my remodelled spacious apartment arranged with luxurious comfort, convenience & free wifi. Immerse yourself in the historical district. Temple Bar, Smock Alley, Trinity College, Museums, Grafton Street shops, all a short walk away. Come make memories here, they'll last a lifetime.
neighborhood_overview: This is the historical part of Dublin, so you will be spoiled for choice. Dublinia is beside Christchurch and is a historical recreation museum, concentrating on Viking and medieval history of the city.  The Guinness Storehouse is well worth a visit.  Dublin Castle is 5 mins away, built in the 13th century.  Of course, Trinity College, Temple Bar, and the shopping area of Grafton Street are just a 10 to 15 minute stroll down through Dame Street passing the Olympia Theatre as you go.  Self hire Dublin bikes are available at Wood Quay, Christchurch Place, should you like to tour Dublin by bike.  In that case I would recommend a ride up to the Phoenix Park, one of the largest Public Parks in Europe and so beautiful, you might catch sight of a deer or a stag.  The Phoenix Park is about a 20 minutes walk, and if you like to get a run in on your break, you would certainly enjoy the sights here.
host_about:
Hello! Why does the idea of talking about oneself strike fear in one's heart, is it that we're just too bashful or the subject matter might be boring, ha.  I'm a mother of two wonderful young adults. I took up running some years ago and have ran many International Marathons including some of the majors New York, Boston, London, Paris, San Francisco all of which I qualified for where necessary.  I'm a glass half full type of person and certainly believe that if plan A doesn't work, there's always plan B, C, etc.,.  I enjoy meeting people and hosting with Airbnb has been a terrific experience for me in that regard.  In general I love to see people enjoying life and if I can help them in that goal, all the better.  I'm a believer in karma and thus each day is an opportunity to do something good and make people happy.  Of course , I have a huge work ethic and I like to give a 100% to whatever I'm working on.  I'm a  cleanliness freak, having had a bad experience in what I thought was a good hotel in London, long story short, I jumped into bed after a long day in London and a late theatre night, in the morning when I woke, I noticed there was a brown coffee stain on my sheet, obviously the sheets had not been changed, I was Not a happy camper!  Who would have thought, needless to say, I check wherever I stay now!   
I love Dublin city and the people, I'm a Dubliner even though my Dad hailed from County Kerry (the California of Ireland), and my Mum from County Westmeath.  I love to pretend to be a tourist in my own city, the things you notice and discover, always something new.  Life always has moments to be recorded, thus the advent of phones with cameras has enabled me to embrace my other passion, photography, I think I have at least 20,000 photos,  thank goodness for iCloud.
Hope all that didn't bore you too much, have a wonderful day, Namaste.:-)

neighborhood_overview:
This is an old traditional "working class" part of town. The houses are cosy and functional - all built in the 1920's. It's famous for the huge Croke Park stadium - the home of the GAA - which hosts 2 big concerts most years and of course many matches most weekends.

It's a very "studenty" part of town being very near to DCU and the Mater Hospital. This means there are plenty of good small restaurants and convenience stores all around.

For a pleasant walk I may recommend the Canal (up by the statue of Brendan Behan) or a great walk via Griffith Park to the Botanic Gardens and onwards to Glasnevin Cemetery.

Drumcondra (as the area is known) was the stomping ground of Bertie Ahern if you're interested in that sort of thing.

neighborhood_overview:
The house is located in Stoneybatter. The neighbourhood has plenty of of old school Dublin character but has been known as an "up-and-coming" part of the city for quite some time now. It is precisely this mixture which makes Stoneybatter appealing to locals and tourists alike.

Apart from the striking red brick artisan dwellings, the area is also known for the prominent Viking street names. For example, there is Viking Road, Olaf Road, Thor Place, Norseman Place, Ard Ri Road, Ostman Place & Sigurd Road. At the time of the Norman invasion, the Vikings, Ostmen or Austmenn (men of the East) as they called themselves, were exiled to the north of the Liffey where they founded the hamlet of Ostmenstown it what is now Stoneybatter.

neighborhood_overview: Howth is an idyllic fishing village on the northeast of Dublin and has been immortalised in James Joyce’s Ulysses. The grounds of 15th-century Howth Castle have rhododendron gardens and a transport museum with local trams. The 19th-century Martello Tower houses a vintage radio museum.  The medieval ruins of St. Mary’s Abbey lie nearby.  A clifftop trail has sweeping sea views, indeed H.G. Wells once remarked that Howth had "the finest views west of Naples".  Offshore, Ireland’s Eye is an island bird sanctuary with an ancient ruined church.  Walk around the working fishing village of Howth to explore the range of food on offer.  Enjoy the best traditional fish and chips in the city or sample some of the finest seafood cuisine all with the added perk of stunning coastal views.

neighborhood_overview:
In Malahide there is something for everyone, shoppers, sports fanatics, day trippers and holiday makers, the picturesque village boasts a wide array of retail destinations and services including fashion boutiques, hair and beauty salons, florists, restaurants, cafes and two small shopping centres.

Traditional shopfronts and several cobble-lock side streets give the village an intimate and welcoming feel. There are a broad range of pubs and restaurants to take you well into the night and a wide range of leisure and sports activities to get you up in the morning.

Malahide’s substantial marina is accessible from an attractive promenade, beginning at Village Green. Walking in the opposite direction will take you to Malahide’s long, sandy beach. Surrounding the town are the protected grounds of Malahide Castle, with botanic gardens, sports pitches and a children’s playground, land which was once the private estate of Baron Talbot.

neighborhood_overview:
The Liberties is considered by many the heart of Dublin as well as being home to the world-famous and Ireland’s most visited tourist attraction – Guinness!

In medieval times Dublin was a walled city with tariffs and taxes charged to protect the city. However, The Liberties, was located just outside the city walls of Norman Dublin making its residents at liberty from the city laws, including the need to pay taxes!

Later, the area became home to a large French Hugenot population along with crafts such as weavers and whiskey distillers.

During the late 18th and 19th century, The Liberties was full of breweries and distilleries, including the Guinness family, who built the now famous site at St James’ Gate in 1759.

Today, it’s Ireland’s most visited tourist attraction and it’s just c400m from the apartment! Meanwhile a recent renaissance in whiskey distillers in The Liberties means there are plenty for whiskey lovers.

description:

neighborhood_overview:
Our home is in historic Raheny Village which is on the coast about 8km (5.0 mi) from Dublin city center and 7km (4.3 mi) from Dublin Airport.
For music and sports fans, the Three Arena is just 7km away, Croke Park Stadium 6km and the Aviva rugby stadium less than 10km.
Two major features of Raheny are the 5 km (3.1 mi) beach known as Dollymount Strand on the nature reserve of Bull Island, and Saint Annes, the largest of Dublin's municipal parks, formerly the home of the Gunness family.
Eight crescent cottages on Station Road near the junction with the Howth Road are among the oldest buildings in the village, having been built around 1790.
There is excellent walking and cycling on the sea front, the Bull Island, in St. Anne's Park and around the local streets.
For golfers, we have the Royal Dublin, Portmarnock, Clontarf and St. Annes Golf Clubs all on our doorstep, with many more close by.

host_about:
Why we are here?

Hotels aren't always hip and hosts aren't always reliable so we’ve spotted a gap where we filter out all the crap. We want to change the game with unique spaces that inspire and that can be remarkable and affordable at the same time.

The Hiphipstay story started back in 2015 when our founder Will McGlade was travelling around the US with his mates. During their travels, vacation rentals were always their first choice over hotels. They loved the added comfort of renting a home in a city or a coastal town and living like a local.

How we got started ?

Will recognised a gap in the homestay market back home Ireland. He wanted to put an end to having to trawl through hundreds of average listings to find something special. So he created a platform that made it simple to rent the absolute best homes available, where hotel meets home.

Where we’re going ?

What began as a journey to provide a better stay has grown into a celebration of modern design and exceptional comfort. We’re working with world-class software developers, hosts and designers to create truly remarkable spaces—ones that transcend hospitality and enrich lives to bring Hiphipstay to be a truly global brand.

neighborhood_overview:
This is an old traditional "working class" part of town. The houses are cosy and functional - all built in the 1920's. It's famous for the huge Croke Park stadium - the home of the GAA - which hosts 2 big concerts most years and of course many matches most weekends.

It's a very "studenty" part of town being very near to DCU and the Mater Hospital. This means there are plenty of good small restaurants and convenience stores all around.

For a pleasant walk I may recommend the Canal (up by the statue of Brendan Behan) or a great walk via Griffith Park to the Botanic Gardens and onwards to Glasnevin Cemetery.

Drumcondra (as the area is known) was the stomping ground of Bertie Ahern if you're interested in that sort of thing.

neighborhood_overview:
Stonybatter is small neighbourhood in Dublin City Centre. The following blurb is from Timeout magazine which included Stonybatter in its 'Top 50' of coolest neighbourhoods in the world.

"This area feels like its own world, a quirky little fortress of cool in the heart of the city. Dubliners who’ve lived here their whole lives now mingle with trendy newcomers clambering to rent one of its cute little cottages. name: Contemporary family home in beautiful Howth
description: Our comfy spacious family home is available to rent this summer. Located on a quiet, leafy cul de sac with a beautiful sandy beach 200m from the door. It’s a 10 minute walk into Howth Village, famous for its many fish restaurants, beautiful cliff walks and beaches. You can rent a kayak, take an off-road bike tour, visit a puffin colony on an uninhabited island all within this small peninsula just a 20 minute journey from Dublin City Centre.
neighborhood_overview:
The house is ideally located, with access to a sandy beach 200m from the door. From here you can walk into Howth or further on to burrow beach if the sea is far enough out. At high tide the beach is largely inaccessible so you may have it all to yourself!

Howth is a gorgeous spot, the village is famous for its seafood restaurants and there is a lovely buzz about the place with many people sitting outside enjoying food and a glass of wine. There are a couple of small museums, a playground and some boutique shops. There are often lots of visitors out walking the pier with a coffee and soaking up the views.

For walking fans the coastline offers a varied mix of cliffs, pebbly beaches and lots of sand, plus there are nice treks through old woods in the middle of the peninsula to summits with views over many counties (and on a good day you can even see Wales!)

There are a variety of water sports on offer - kayaking, yachting, diving, stand up paddle board....
host_about:

My house is in CRUMLIN, ALTHOUGH probably best known internationally as the childhood home of Conor McGregor, is in fact one of Dublin’s oldest closest suburbs to Dublin city centre. Taking its name from the ‘crooked glen’ - croimghlinn – of the river Camac that is now Lansdowne Valley Park, it was a recognised settlement before the Norman conquest in 1170.
Crumlin immediately has one up on any other part of Dublin – this is Phil Lynott country. His mam’s house is just around the corner. neighborhood_overview:
Saint Kevin’s is known for buzzing nightlife, with a live music scene ranging from Irish folk bands in traditional pubs to dance club DJ sets and symphonies at the 19th-century National Concert Hall. Chic bistros and gastrobars stand alongside casual noodle and burger joints. The area is named for its neo-Gothic parish church and centred on Iveagh Gardens, a classical landscaped park with a waterfall and a yew maze.

Next to the apartment complex there is barber, laundrette and corner shop. Directly across the road you will find The Bean Roastery coffee shop, McCauleys Pharamcy, Ashai Asian restaurant and takeout, Krewe, a New Orleans inspired restaurant and a large Tesco express supermarket.

On the corner of Charlemont Street is McCaffertys pub looking onto the Dublin canal which serves food all day. The trendy village of Ranelagh, and Iveagh Gardens are both a 5 minute walk away (in opposite directions!) and it’s a 10minute walk to St. Stephens Green and Grafto

Seasoned traveller, lived in Australia for 7 years, living in Dublin City the last 3 years.  When I'm not working I like to check out new restaurants, go to  concerts, watch films, appreciate art and shop! 

I love exploring new places and cultures and I’m always trying to fit in a hike or a relaxing day in a spa!

The centre of Dublin has a very organic feel to it, with its winding, narrow streets and low buildings. There is only one grand avenue in the centre and that is O'Connell Street. The rest of the streets is much more human in scale. Few buildings in the city centre are more than four stories high and an appealing mix of 18th century Georgian and 19th century Victorian styles dominates most streets in the centre. Life in Dublin's city centre is charming, slightly chaotic and fairly laid back.

Dublin's Hub
Dublin City CentreDublin has a hub and spokes structure, with the centre as the hub and outlying areas as the spokes. Because of the relatively small size of Dublin, most fresh impulses and ideas start in the centre to reach the biggest possible audience. New shops, bars and nightclubs invariably operate from a city centre location and there are still enough up and coming areas waiting to be discovered, which keeps rents low for innovative start-ups. neighborhood_overview:
Rialto is an old area of Dublin with long connections to industry. The original canal was constructed to serve the Guinness brewery, and much of Rialto Street and Rialto Cottages were built to house Guinness employees at the tail end of the 19th century. These developments gave the area a redbrick character which it keeps to this day.

In the middle of the 20th century, it became home to two of Dublin Corporation’s large-scale housing projects, Dolphin House and Fatima Mansions. The latter became a byword for failed inner-city development and was eventually demolished in the early 2000s; Dolphin House is currently undergoing extensive regeneration works.

In common with the rest of Dublin 8, recent years have seen an influx of younger renters and buyers who mix with residents of several generations’ standing.

With much of the city being built up with cookie-cutter hotels and skyscrapers, this nook has retained much of its original architecture. The neighbourhood features a number of bars, cultural venues, distilleries, shops and cafes.

Generations of inner city folk infuse its street life with their quick-witted character, while new generations are welcomed in to live, work and play in this ever-evolving neighbourhood.

Dense with history, it retains deep-rooted traditions, yet it sits on the cusp of Dublin’s future too, hosting the Digital Hub, where tomorrow’s disruptors are today’s start-ups, and the sprawling Guinness brewery, founded by Arthur Guinness in 1759. It’s even the site of ambitious plans for a new cultural quarter.

The local convenience shop is a 10 minute walk as well as Ryans Victorian Bar&Restaurant.

neighborhood_overview:
The main entrance to the Phoenix Park, via Parkgate Street, is on your doorstep and it is the largest enclosed public park in any capital city in Europe. There is more than 700 hectares to explore and not only does the the President of Ireland live there in "The Aras", but it's also home to Dublin Zoo, has play grounds for the kids, polo and cricket grounds, cycle paths and bike rental, coffee shops, as well as a large herd of fallow deer that still call it home.
Stoneybatter is your local neighbourhood for hanging out in. Situated on the Northside of the River Liffey, it's one of the last genuine inner city urban villages, where old Dublin meets new development, but still has a strong community spirit and a local feel. Manor Street has become a foodie hub shared with artists and crafters and can boast its own publishing house and bookshop, Liliput Press (their namesake coffee and deli should not be missed!)
Parkgate Street is a 6 minute walk for your immediate shopping

neighborhood_overview:

Whether you're interested in exploring the city's historical landmarks, sampling the local cuisine, or experiencing the famous Irish nightlife, Dublin has something to offer for everyone.

One of the most popular attractions in Dublin is Trinity College, which is home to the famous Book of Kells. This 9th-century manuscript is a must-see for any history lover. Another historical landmark not to be missed is Dublin Castle, which dates back to the 13th century and has played a key role in the city's history. Both are located within a 5 minute walk of the property.

Originally settled as an ‘estate village’ to serve the owners of Rathfarnham Castle, the area was properly settled as a suburb in the 1960s and 1970s and has continued to attract families searching for homes surrounded by ample greenery and modern amenities within easy reach of Dublin city.

This friendly community is home to a wide array of restaurants, cafes and pubs, including the famous Yellow House where – according to legend – the architects of the 1798 rebellion met for a dram or two. Both Rathfarnham Shopping Centre and Nutgrove Shopping Centre cater to residents and account for a Tesco, ALDI and Lidl between them. As for schools, there is an excellent choice of both primary and secondary in the area.

name: 2 bed with Superking in D4 - Brookman Town Homes
description: Welcome to Brookman Town Homes.  We have 22 houses in Donnybrook Manor (a mix of 2, 3 and 4 bedroom houses).  Our 2 bed townhouses are 680 sq. ft. and  have a double bedroom and a twin room (or Superking if you prefer!).  You will also find WiFi, access to 100 TV channels/Netflix, and a complimentary breakfast welcome pack upon arrival in each house. Our properties also include parking and a private garden.  Located right in the heart of exclusive Donnybrook Village it's the perfect location.
neighborhood_overview:
Arguably one of Dublin's finest neighbourhoods. Donnybrook Manor is tucked away in a quiet residential estate behind Donnybrook Village. Donnybrook has number of high end independent clothing boutiques (Havanna, Marian Gayle), food stores (Donnybrook Fair, Tesco) , restaurants (Marco Pierre Whites), pubs (The Morehampton) and speciality cafes including The Natural Bakery Company, Happy Out Coffee, Butlers and Nero Coffee. There is a bus stop around the corner which will bring you straight into town in a few minutes (or UCD/Dun Laoghaire etc in the other direction).

The stunning Herbert Park is just a short stroll away and is adorned by pink cherry blossom trees in the Spring. It has a farmers market with food from around the world on a Sunday morning. It boasts 3 playgrounds and a duck pond for the little ones. It also has pay as you play tennis (rent rackets in Lolly & Cookes cafe), astro pitches, soccer pitches and exercise equipment for joggers.

host_about:
Why we are here?

Hotels aren't always hip and hosts aren't always reliable so we’ve spotted a gap where we filter out all the crap. We want to change the game with unique spaces that inspire and that can be remarkable and affordable at the same time.

The Hiphipstay story started back in 2015 when our founder Will McGlade was travelling around the US with his mates. During their travels, vacation rentals were always their first choice over hotels. They loved the added comfort of renting a home in a city or a coastal town and living like a local.

How we got started ?

Will recognised a gap in the homestay market back home Ireland. He wanted to put an end to having to trawl through hundreds of average listings to find something special. So he created a platform that made it simple to rent the absolute best homes available, where hotel meets home.

Where we’re going ?

What began as a journey to provide a better stay has grown into a celebration of modern design and exceptional comfort. We’re working with world-class software developers, hosts and designers to create truly remarkable spaces—ones that transcend hospitality and enrich lives to bring Hiphipstay to be a truly global brand.

Christchurch is one of Dublin’s most historic and atmospheric neighbourhoods—an unbeatable base for exploring the city. With cobbled streets, medieval architecture, and the majestic Christ Church Cathedral at its heart, this area blends old-world charm with modern city buzz.

Great transport links, cosy pubs, riverside walks, and a rich cultural history make Christchurch the perfect spot for travellers who want to soak up Dublin’s spirit while enjoying the convenience of staying right in the centre of it all.
